```{r}
    data.frame(rows = d$rows[1L], cache = d$cache[1L], forms = length(first_t), interleaved = length(first_t) > 1L && max(first_t) < min(last_t),
               own_inside = any(to >= min(t) & to <= max(t_end)), has_own = nrow(o) > 0L, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  rw_split <- has_cf && !any(cell_chk$own_inside)
  dr <- rw_get("dplyr_rowwise", min(rw_sizes), "warm"); cu0 <- rw_get("cuplyr_rowwise", min(rw_sizes), "warm")
  dr_x <- if (nrow(dr) && nrow(cu0) && dr$n > 0L && cu0$n > 0L) dr$med / cu0$med else NA_real_
  four_sizes <- sort(unique(cell_chk$rows[!cell_chk$has_own]))
  shared_forms <- setdiff(rw_forms, "dplyr_rowwise")
  rw_cells_text <- if (!rw_split) "In this data set dplyr rowwise shared its cells with the other forms, so a cuplyr call could follow one of its long calls." else paste0(
    "A size in a cache state makes two cells, run one after the other with the same cache control, check, cap and load rule. dplyr rowwise is timed in a cell of its own: ",
    if (!is.na(dr_x)) paste0("at ", lab_n(min(rw_sizes)), " rows (warm cache) its median call takes ", fs(dr$med), ", ", format(round(dr_x), big.mark = ","), " times cuplyr rowwise's, ") else "",
    "so in a shared cell each of its calls would leave the GPU idle for that long between two cuplyr calls, and an idle GPU makes the next cuplyr call slower (see Findings). ",
    "The other forms (", join_and(rw_label[shared_forms]), ") are timed together in the other cell, interleaved: their start times interleave in ", sum(cell_chk$interleaved), " of the ", nrow(cell_chk),
    " such cells, and no dplyr rowwise call started while one of them ran (both checked in `rowwise.csv`)",
    if (length(four_sizes)) paste0(". At ", join_and(lab_n(four_sizes)), " rows dplyr rowwise was not run (it had been capped at a smaller size), so there the shared cell is the only one and has four forms") else "",
    ". The ratios against dplyr rowwise below compare medians from the two cells of a size and cache state.")

  # the gaps before cuplyr's timed rowwise calls, against the idle probe
  rcg <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(cu_rows, paste(cu_rows$rows, cu_rows$cache)), gap_of))
  rcq <- rcg[rcg$rep >= 1L & rcg$ok & rcg$quiet, ]
  rw_gap_max <- max(rcq$gap, na.rm = TRUE)
  rw_gap_text <- paste0(
    "Every quiet cuplyr rep came at most ", fx(rw_gap_max, 1), " seconds after cuplyr's previous call in its cell",
    if (!have_idle) "." else if (rw_gap_max <= idle_safe) paste0(", within the ", idle_safe, " seconds of idle after which the idle probe saw no slowdown.")
    else paste0("; ", sum(rcq$gap > idle_safe, na.rm = TRUE), " came more than the ", idle_safe, " seconds of idle after which the idle probe saw no slowdown, and their times may include it."))

  # the earlier measurement, archived when the chunk was re-timed. Built in local(): only
  # the paragraph leaves it, so its working names cannot replace a name the prose uses
  if (!is.null(rwsup) && nrow(rwsup)) rw_sup_text <- local({
    rwsup$ok <- as.logical(rwsup$ok); rwsup$quiet <- as.logical(rwsup$quiet)
    old_shared <- if ("cell_forms" %in% names(rwsup)) is.na(rwsup$cell_forms) | !nzchar(rwsup$cell_forms) else rep(TRUE, nrow(rwsup))
    os <- rwsup[which(old_shared & rwsup$form == "cuplyr_rowwise" & rwsup$rep >= 1L & rwsup$ok & rwsup$quiet & rwsup$rows == min(rw_sizes)), ]
    old_med <- vapply(c("warm", "cold"), function(cc) { x <- os$secs[os$cache == cc]; if (length(x)) stats::median(x) else NA_real_ }, 0)
    new_med <- vapply(c("warm", "cold"), function(cc) { x <- rw_get("cuplyr_rowwise", min(rw_sizes), cc); if (nrow(x) && x$n > 0L) x$med else NA_real_ }, 0)
    # each archived row's run: the superseded rowwise step whose window it started in
    pv_rw_old <- pv[pv$step == "rowwise" & pv$superseded, ]
    sup_t <- tstamp(rwsup$started)
    rwsup$head <- vapply(seq_along(sup_t), function(i) {
      j <- which(pv_rw_old$t0 <= sup_t[i] & pv_rw_old$t1 >= sup_t[i]); if (length(j)) pv_rw_old$git_head[j[1L]] else NA_character_
    }, "")
    # a form that was not run has no start time: its run is the run of the rows archived with it
    # (the driver stamps every row of a replaced piece with the same superseded_at)
    if ("superseded_at" %in% names(rwsup)) {
      at_head <- tapply(rwsup$head, rwsup$superseded_at, function(h) { h <- unique(h[!is.na(h)]); if (length(h) == 1L) h else NA_character_ })
      miss <- is.na(rwsup$head)
      rwsup$head[miss] <- unname(at_head[rwsup$superseded_at[miss]])
    }
    n_unmatched <- sum(is.na(rwsup$head))
    sup_heads <- unique(rwsup$head[!is.na(rwsup$head)])
    # the same method as the data in use: dplyr rowwise in cells of its own; the latest such run is the replicate
    same_heads <- unique(rwsup$head[!old_shared & !is.na(rwsup$head)])
    rw_rep_text <- ""
    if (length(same_heads)) {
      rep_head <- same_heads[length(same_heads)]
      rp <- rwsup[rwsup$head %in% rep_head, ]
      rpq <- rp[rp$rep >= 1L & rp$ok & rp$quiet, ]
      rp_med <- tapply(rpq$secs, rw_key(rpq), stats::median)
      rp_stat <- tapply(rp$status, rw_key(rp), function(x) { bad <- x[x != "ok"]; if (length(bad)) bad[[1L]] else "ok" })
      cur <- RS[RS$status == "ok" & RS$n > 0L, ]
      cur$old <- unname(rp_med[cur$key])
      both <- cur[!is.na(cur$old), ]
      # verdict 1: per size and cache state, the form with the lowest median among the forms with a median in both runs
      lowest <- function(col) vapply(split(both, paste(both$rows, both$cache)), function(z) z$form[which.min(z[[col]])], "")
      b_new <- lowest("med"); b_old <- lowest("old")[names(b_new)]
      n_best_same <- sum(b_new == b_old)
      # verdict 2: cuplyr rowwise faster or slower than each other form
      side <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(both, paste(both$rows, both$cache)), function(z) {
        cu <- z[z$form == "cuplyr_rowwise", ]; ot <- z[z$form != "cuplyr_rowwise", ]
        if (!nrow(cu) || !nrow(ot)) return(NULL)
        data.frame(form = ot$form, rows = ot$rows, cache = ot$cache, new = cu$med / ot$med, old = cu$old / ot$old, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      }))
      if (is.null(side)) side <- data.frame(form = character(), rows = numeric(), cache = character(), new = numeric(), old = numeric())
      n_side_same <- sum((side$new < 1) == (side$old < 1))
      # verdict 3: the same cells capped or not run (the not-run rows matched above included)
      st_keys <- intersect(RS$key, names(rp_stat))
      n_stat_same <- sum(unname(rp_stat[st_keys]) == RS$status[match(st_keys, RS$key)])
      agrees <- n_best_same == length(b_new) && n_side_same == nrow(side) && n_stat_same == length(st_keys)
      # cuplyr at the smallest size (warm), and its ratio to DuckDB at the largest size both runs have (warm)
      cu_old_small <- rp_med[paste("cuplyr_rowwise", min(rw_sizes), "warm", sep = "|")]
      dk <- side[side$form == "duckdb" & side$cache == "warm", ]
      dk <- dk[dk$rows == max(dk$rows), ]
      # the spread between the runs: the largest difference of a median, and the rest
      both$rel <- abs(both$old / both$med - 1)
      both$outside <- both$old < both$q25 | both$old > both$q75
      top <- which.max(both$rel); ex <- both[top, ]
      rest_rel <- if (nrow(both) > 1L) max(both$rel[-top]) else NA_real_
      # the chance that a replicate median lies outside this run's interquartile range if both runs
      # are draws from one distribution: the pooled quiet reps of a form, size and cache state, split
      # between the runs in every possible way (up to max_splits ways) or else in n_perm random ways
      # (a fixed seed; the session's random state is put back afterwards)
      n_perm <- 4000L; max_splits <- 1000
      seed_old <- if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE)) get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else NULL
      set.seed(121L)
      chance <- do.call(rbind, lapply(both$key, function(k) {
        x <- rwq$secs[rw_key(rwq) == k]; pool <- c(x, rpq$secs[rw_key(rpq) == k]); nx <- length(x)
        outside <- function(i) {
          q <- stats::quantile(pool[i], c(0.25, 0.75), names = FALSE); m <- stats::median(pool[-i])
          m < q[1L] || m > q[2L]
        }
        every <- choose(length(pool), nx) <= max_splits
        p <- if (every) mean(apply(utils::combn(length(pool), nx), 2L, outside)) else mean(vapply(seq_len(n_perm), function(b) outside(sample.int(length(pool), nx)), NA))
        data.frame(nx = nx, ny = length(pool) - nx, every = every, p = p)
      }))
      if (is.null(seed_old)) rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) else assign(".Random.seed", seed_old, envir = globalenv())
      n_out <- sum(both$outside)
      exp_out <- sum(chance$p)
      # the count's distribution, the cells taken as independent (a Poisson-binomial), and its upper tail
      dist <- 1
      for (p in chance$p) dist <- c(dist * (1 - p), 0) + c(0, dist * p)
      p_out <- sum(dist[(n_out + 1L):length(dist)])
      split_of <- function(z) join_or(unique(sprintf("%d and %d reps", z$nx, z$ny)))
      spread_text <- if (!nrow(both)) "No median has quiet reps in both runs" else paste0(
        "The largest difference between the runs is for ", rw_label[[ex$form]], " at ", lab_n(ex$rows), " rows (", ex$cache, " cache): ", fs(ex$old), " there against ", fs(ex$med), " here, ",
        pct1(ex$rel), " apart and ", if (ex$outside) "outside" else "inside", " this run's interquartile range (", fnum(ex$q25), "-", fnum(ex$q75), " s)",
        if (!is.na(rest_rel)) paste0("; the other ", nrow(both) - 1L, " medians (a form at a size and cache state) differ by ", pct1(rest_rel), " or less") else "",
        ". The replicate's median lies outside this run's interquartile range in ", n_out, " of the ", nrow(both), ". If the two runs were draws from one distribution, about ", fx(exp_out, 1),
        " would, and ", n_out, " or more would with a chance of ", pct(p_out), " (from splitting the pooled quiet reps of each form, size and cache state between the two runs: ",
        join_and(c(if (any(chance$every)) paste0("every possible split for a cell of ", split_of(chance[chance$every, ])),
                   if (any(!chance$every)) paste0(format(n_perm, big.mark = ","), " random splits for a cell of ", split_of(chance[!chance$every, ])))),
        "). So the count gives ", if (p_out >= 0.05) "no sign that the runs differ by more than the spread within one run" else "a sign that the runs differ by more than the spread within one run")
      rw_rep_text <- paste0(
        ". The ", if (length(sup_heads) == 2L) "second" else "last", " of them, from benchmark commit `", rep_head, "`, timed dplyr rowwise in cells of its own, as the data in use do, and so is a replicate of them. ",
        if (agrees) "It agrees on every verdict: " else "It does not agree on every verdict: ",
        "in ", n_best_same, " of the ", length(b_new), " combinations of size and cache state the same form has the lowest median among the forms with a median in both runs, in ",
        n_side_same, " of the ", nrow(side), " comparisons with another form cuplyr rowwise is faster in both runs or slower in both, and ", n_stat_same, " of the ", length(st_keys), " combinations of form, size and cache state in both runs have the same status (",
        join_or(gsub("_", " ", sort(unique(c(RS$status[match(st_keys, RS$key)], unname(rp_stat[st_keys])))), fixed = TRUE)), ")",
        if (n_unmatched) paste0("; ", n_of(n_unmatched, "archived row"), " match no run and ", if (n_unmatched == 1L) "is" else "are", " left out") else "", ". ",
        "cuplyr's median at ", lab_n(min(rw_sizes)), " rows (warm cache) was ", fs(cu_old_small), " there and ", fs(new_med[["warm"]]), " here",
        if (nrow(dk)) paste0(", and its ratio to DuckDB at ", lab_n(dk$rows), " rows (warm cache) ", fx(dk$old, 2), " there and ", fx(dk$new, 2), " here") else "", ". ",
        spread_text)
    }
    paste0(
      "Earlier runs of this chunk are kept in `rowwise-superseded.csv` (", nrow(rwsup), " rows) and not used",
      if (any(old_shared) && !any(is.na(old_med)) && !any(is.na(new_med))) paste0(
        ". The first of them timed dplyr rowwise in the same cells as the other forms, and there cuplyr's median at ", lab_n(min(rw_sizes)), " rows was ", fs(old_med[["warm"]]), " (warm) and ", fs(old_med[["cold"]]),
        " (cold), ", fx(old_med[["warm"]] / new_med[["warm"]], 1), " and ", fx(old_med[["cold"]] / new_med[["cold"]], 1), " times the medians above") else "", rw_rep_text, ".")
  })
}
rw_ratio_cell <- function(r) {
  if (!is.na(r$ratio)) fnum(r$ratio) else if (!is.na(r$bound)) paste0("< ", fnum(r$bound), " (capped)")
  else if (r$other_status == "not_run") "not run" else "n/a"
}
rw_cell_text <- function(d) {
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) {
    x <- d[i, ]
    cs <- if (length(cap_size) && x$form %in% names(cap_size)) cap_size[[x$form]] else NA_real_
    switch(x$status,
      ok = sprintf("%s (%s-%s) n=%d", fnum(x$med), fnum(x$q25), fnum(x$q75), x$n),
      capped = paste0("capped: a call ran over ", fnum(rw_cap), " s",
                      if (length(cap_at) && x$key %in% names(cap_at) && !is.na(cap_at[[x$key]])) paste0(" (aborted at ", fnum(cap_at[[x$key]]), " s)") else "",
                      if (x$n > 0L) sprintf(" (%d quiet reps before)", x$n) else ""),
      not_run = paste0("not run: capped at ", if (is.na(cs)) "a smaller size" else paste(lab_n(cs), "rows")),
      oom = "does not fit", noisy = "no quiet rep", x$status)
  }, "")
}
rw_tab <- function(cache) {
  d <- RS[RS$cache == cache, ]
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
  rows <- lapply(sort(unique(d$rows)), function(n) {
    r <- d[d$rows == n, ]
    usable <- r$status == "ok" & r$n > 0L
    best <- if (any(usable)) r$form[usable][which.min(r$med[usable])] else NA_character_
    txt <- rw_cell_text(r)
    cells <- vapply(rw_forms, function(f) { i <- match(f, r$form); if (is.na(i)) "-" else if (identical(f, best)) paste0("**", txt[[i]], "**") else txt[[i]] }, "")
    out <- data.frame(rows = lab_n(n), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    for (f in rw_forms) out[[rw_label[[f]]]] <- cells[[f]]
    out
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
rw_cols_pal <- c(`cuplyr rowwise` = "#009E73", `dplyr rowwise` = "#0072B2", `dplyr vectorised` = "#56B4E9", `data.table vectorised` = "#CC79A7", DuckDB = "#E69F00")
plot_rowwise <- function() {
  d <- RS[RS$status == "ok" & RS$n > 0L, ]
  if (!nrow(d)) return(invisible(NULL))
  d$form <- factor(rw_label[d$form], rw_label)
  d$cache <- factor(d$cache, c("warm", "cold"))
  g <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x = rows, y = med, colour = form, group = form)) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(ggplot2::aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), alpha = 0.6) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.8) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_log10(breaks = rw_sizes, labels = lab_n(rw_sizes)) + ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = rw_cols_pal, drop = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~cache, nrow = 1, labeller = ggplot2::label_both) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "rows in the wide table", y = "seconds per call (median, bars = interquartile range)", colour = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
  cp <- RS[RS$status == "capped", ]; nr <- RS[RS$status == "not_run", ]
  mk <- function(z) { z$form <- factor(rw_label[z$form], rw_label); z$cache <- factor(z$cache, c("warm", "cold")); z$y <- rw_cap; z }
  if (nrow(cp)) g <- g + ggplot2::geom_point(data = mk(cp), ggplot2::aes(x = rows, y = y, colour = form), shape = 4, size = 3.5, stroke = 1.3, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  if (nrow(nr)) g <- g + ggplot2::geom_point(data = mk(nr), ggplot2::aes(x = rows, y = y, colour = form), shape = 1, size = 3.5, stroke = 1.1, inherit.aes = FALSE)
  if (nrow(cp) || nrow(nr)) {
    marks <- c(if (nrow(cp)) paste0("a cross marks a cell capped at ", fnum(rw_cap), " seconds"),
               if (nrow(nr)) "a circle a form not run at that size (it was capped at a smaller one)")
    g <- g + ggplot2::labs(caption = paste0(paste(marks, collapse = ", "),
                                            if (length(marks) > 1L) "; both are drawn at the cap" else ", drawn at the cap"))
  }
  g
}
rw_caveat <- if (!have_rw) "It is not part of this data set." else paste0(
  "Its sizes (", join_and(lab_n(rw_sizes)), " rows) are smaller than the main pipelines' because dplyr's per-row route is slow; the cap of ", rw_cap_text, " per call was chosen before the run, and a capped cell is a lower bound on that form's time, not a measurement. ",
  "The four double columns are fillers with few distinct values, the wide table is the same synthetic table as in the other pipelines",
  if (nrow(rw_only_files)) paste0(" (the file at ", join_and(lab_n(rw_only_files$rows)), " rows, used only here, comes from the same generator and seed)") else "",
  ", and the forms are one author's reading of each engine's natural style. ",
  "The rowwise forms ran in one shared process too, like the main pipelines; there data.table's median in the shared process was ", fx(shared_med[["data.table"]], 2),
  " times its median in a process of its own (the process-effects caveat), and its rowwise numbers ", if (shared_med[["data.table"]] > 1.2) "may be high in the same way" else "are not expected to differ much", " (not measured for the rowwise pipeline).")
```

## Setup

### Machine and software

All numbers come from one machine: a `r cpu_model` with `r n_cpu` logical CPUs and `r ram_gb` GB of RAM, and a `r gpu_name` with `r gpu_gb` GB of memory. `r disk_text` Versions: cuplyr `r ver_cuplyr` (package code at commit `r join_and(pkg_commits)`, libcudf `r ver_cudf`), DuckDB `r ver_duckdb`, dplyr `r ver_dplyr`, arrow `r ver_arrow`, data.table `r ver_dt`, R `r ver_r`. cuplyr is loaded from the checkout with `pkgload::load_all()`; nothing is installed.

### Provenance

The driver appends a row to `provenance.csv` for every step it runs: the benchmark code's commit, whether `bench/` had uncommitted changes, the commit of the package code and whether it was modified, and the start and end of the step. The steps that take timings refuse to run with uncommitted changes in `bench/`. The `r nrow(pvu)` step runs whose data are in use ran `r span_text`, from `r heads_text` and package commit `r join_and(pkg_commits)`; `r if (all_clean) "none of them ran with uncommitted changes" else "some ran with uncommitted changes"`, and `r if (all_ok) "every one ended ok" else "some did not end ok"`. `r if (n_pv_super) paste0(n_of(n_pv_super, "earlier step run"), " of the same step and piece ", was_were(n_pv_super), " replaced by a later run (marked in the table; the replaced timing rows are archived and not used).") else "No step run was replaced by a later one."` The timings are the `r nrow(time_pieces)` time steps (one size, table and cache each); `r n_pieces_rerun` of them ran more than once, and `r n_of(n_super, "timing row")` `r was_were(n_super)` superseded (`timings-superseded.csv` keeps any attempt that a re-run replaces).

```{r}
#| label: provenance-table
pt <- data.frame(step = pv$step, piece = prov_label(pv), started = format(pv$t0, if (same_day) "%H:%M:%S" else "%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), minutes = fx(pv$minutes, 1),
                 `benchmark commit` = pv$git_head, `bench/ clean` = !as.logical(pv$bench_dirty),
                 `package commit` = pv$cuplyr_commit, `package clean` = !as.logical(pv$cuplyr_dirty),
                 `in use` = ifelse(pv$superseded, "no: run again later", "yes"), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(pt, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

### Data

The data are synthetic and seeded, written once with arrow (`ParquetFileWriter`, snappy compression: the codec in `files.csv` is `r codec`, row groups of `r rg_rows` rows, the last one shorter). The narrow table has `r ncol_of("narrow")` columns: `day` (a Date, sorted ascending, like an event log), `store`, `product` and `qty` (integers), `price` and `discount` (doubles; `discount` has missing values), `channel` and `category` (strings). The wide table has the same columns with identical values plus the filler columns `x01` to `x32` (integers and doubles with few distinct values), `r ncol_of("wide")` columns in all; a pipeline reads at most `r max(lengths(lapply(variants$variant, pp_columns)))` of them. A dimension file `stores.parquet` maps `store` to `region`. `r if (nrow(rw_only_files)) paste0("The rowwise pipeline (see its section) also reads the wide table at ", join_and(lab_n(rw_only_files$rows)), " rows, a file the main pipelines do not use, written by the same generator with the same seed.") else ""`

```{r}
#| label: files-table
ft <- data.frame(table = files$table, rows = lab_n(files$rows), `size in MB` = mb(files$bytes),
                 `row groups` = files$row_groups, codec = files$codec, columns = files$columns, check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(ft, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

### Pipelines

Three pipelines, each with two filters, make six variants (`p1_push`, `p1_nopush`, and so on).

```{r}
#| label: pipelines
#| results: asis
for (p in names(pipe_desc)) cat("- `", p, "`: ", pipe_desc[[p]], "\n", sep = "")
cat("\n")
```

The **push** filter is on the Date and the integer column (`day` on or after `r format(k_const$day_from)` and `qty` at least `r k_const$qty_min`). cuplyr moves such filters into the parquet scan (they are pushed), so row groups whose statistics rule them out are never read. The **nopush** filter is on the double and the string column (`price` at least `r k_const$price_min` and `channel` not `r k_const$channel_drop`); cuplyr never pushes those. The two keep a similar share of the rows (`r pct(keep_frac("push"))` and `r pct(keep_frac("nopush"))`), but they are not the same amount of work for an engine, and the CPU engines show it (see the pushdown section). Because `day` is sorted, the pushed date filter can skip whole row groups; how many row groups each pushed filter really skipped is in the pushdown table below.

### Engines and their code

Each engine is written the way its users write it, and reads only the columns the variant needs.

**cuplyr** reads with `read_parquet_gpu()`, which is lazy by default: the projection and the pushed filter go into the scan. The verbs build a plan (the function below). For the first and second pipelines the final `summarise()` runs the plan at the moment it is called, because `max()` of an integer column has a result type that depends on the data (F07), and `collect()` then only transfers the result to R; for the third pipeline `collect()` runs the plan (`r n_cu_early` of cuplyr's `r n_cu_cells` cells are of the first two kinds). The option `cuplyr.fallback = "error"` makes a CPU fallback an error, so every number is a GPU number: `r sum(tm$engine == "cuplyr" & tm$status == "error")` of cuplyr's `r sum(tm$engine == "cuplyr")` calls in `timings.csv` ended with an error.

```{r}
#| label: code-cuplyr
#| results: asis
code_block(src_of(pp_cuplyr_plan))
```

**DuckDB** keeps one in-memory connection per process (`duckdb(shared_home = FALSE)`), opened before timing like a package load. The query is SQL over `read_parquet('<path>')` with explicit columns, fetched with `dbGetQuery()`. It is SQL rather than dbplyr or duckplyr because that is what a DuckDB user writes. Three of the six queries:

```{r}
#| label: code-duckdb
#| results: asis
for (v in c("p1_push", "p2_nopush", "p3_push")) code_block(pp_sql(v, "<fact>.parquet", "<stores>.parquet"), "sql")
```

**dplyr** reads with `arrow::read_parquet(path, col_select = cols)` and runs the same verbs on the tibble.

```{r}
#| label: code-dplyr
#| results: asis
code_block(src_of(pp_dplyr))
```

**data.table** uses the same reader, then `setDT()` and data.table syntax. `r form_sentence` `r form_p2_sentence`

```{r}
#| label: code-datatable
#| results: asis
code_block(src_of(pp_datatable))
```

None of the results is sorted inside the timed region (dplyr's `summarise()` sorts, DuckDB does not); the comparison sorts them.

### Threads and other settings

Every engine runs at its default thread count, read back from the running engine: `r thread_text`. `r cores_text`

The settings that bear on what a timing means were read back from the running engines into `threads.csv` (the machine and version rows are in the text above):

```{r}
#| label: settings-table
st <- th[!(th$engine == "machine") & !(th$setting %in% c("version", "arrow_version", "git_head")), c("engine", "setting", "value", "step")]
knitr::kable(st, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

DuckDB's `cache_local_files` is `r setting("duckdb", "cache_local_files")` and `enable_external_file_cache` is `r setting("duckdb", "enable_external_file_cache")`, so with these settings DuckDB keeps no copy of a local file between queries and warm and cold mean the operating system's page cache for it too. libcudf's debug stream pool, which cuplyr's `.onLoad` switches on by default (`LIBCUDF_USE_DEBUG_STREAM_POOL`), read back as `r setting("cuplyr", "debug_stream_pool")` in the timing process.

### The parquet reader of dplyr and data.table

dplyr and data.table read with `r reader_used`. The `readers` step timed `arrow::read_parquet(path, col_select = cols)` and `nanoparquet::read_parquet(path, col_select = cols)` on the columns of the first variant, on every table and size with a warm cache: `r reader_sentence`. `r reader_agree_text`

### How the calls were timed

- One **cell** is a variant on a table at a size in a cache state; there are `r n_cells_t` cells. All engines run in every cell, taking turns in a rotating order; the start times of all engines interleave in `r n_interleaved` of the `r n_cells_t` cells (checked in `timings.csv`). No cell and no engine has a different rule: the limit on other processes' load is `r join_and(pct(busy_max_rows))` on every call (recorded per row), and `r if (all(cell_limits == 1L)) "every cell has a single value of it" else "cells differ in it"`. After the first call, each engine takes the number of quiet reps its size needs (`r rep_text`). An untimed `gc()` precedes every call. Every timed result is compared, untimed, with the reference.
- **Warm-up**: before the first cell of each size, table and cache (`r wu_pieces` pieces), every engine ran every variant `r wu_calls` times, untimed (`warmup.csv`, `r nrow(wu)` calls in all, for all `r wu_variants` variants), so one-time costs fall before the timed cells. The first call in a cell (the rep numbered zero in `timings.csv`) is still recorded for every engine and kept out of the medians. The first timed rep takes `r fx(min(rep1_med), 2)` to `r fx(max(rep1_med), 2)` times its cell's median, by engine (the largest single ratio is `r fx(rep1_top$ratio, 2)`, for `r rep1_top$engine`).
- **Warm**: the files are read into the page cache before the cell, and `fincore` checks their residency before every call (lowest `r pct(min(resident_warm))`). **Cold**: before every call the files are `fsync`ed and dropped with `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)`, and `fincore` shows what is left (highest `r pct(max(resident_cold))`).
- **Quiet machine**: one rule for every engine, rep and cache state. The CPU time of the machine's `/proc/stat` is split, over each call, into this process's own time, other processes' user time (the **foreign** share), and kernel time (system, irq and softirq time that this process's own system time does not account for). A call is quiet when its foreign share is at most `r pct(busy_max)`. The wait before each call, which samples the machine for `r fx(stats::median(tm$wait_secs), 2)` seconds with the benchmark idle, uses the same limit. Kernel time is recorded in `timings.csv` but is not part of the rule. A call that is not quiet stays in the raw data, flagged, and is run again (up to a fixed multiple of the reps per engine). Of the `r nrow(timed)` timed calls, `r n_busy` `r was_were(n_busy)` not quiet, and `r n_of(wait_gave_up, "wait")` gave up before the machine was quiet; the highest foreign share in any quiet call is `r pct1(busy_quiet_max)`. `r n_of(n_super, "row")` `r was_were(n_super)` superseded by a re-run. Each piece ran under the GPU lock (`tools/r`), so no other GPU job ran while it did; CPU work outside the lock is not excluded, and only its user-space time would show as foreign load (a compile's system time would show as kernel time, which is outside the rule).
- Medians, quartiles and counts below are over the quiet reps only. A classed out-of-memory error is recorded as such and shown as "does not fit".

The shares during the timed calls, by engine and cache state (median and highest single call, as a share of all `r n_cpu` logical CPUs):

```{r}
#| label: load-table
lt <- data.frame(engine = load_tab$engine, cache = load_tab$cache, calls = load_tab$calls,
                 `foreign (median / highest)` = paste(pct1(load_tab$foreign_med), "/", pct1(load_tab$foreign_max)),
                 `kernel (median / highest)` = paste(pct1(load_tab$kernel_med), "/", pct1(load_tab$kernel_max)),
                 `own CPU as cores (median / highest)` = paste(fx(load_tab$own_med * n_cpu_num, 1), "/", fx(load_tab$own_max * n_cpu_num, 1)),
                 check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(lt, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

`r foreign_sentence` The median kernel share is higher on a cold cache than on a warm one for `r if (any(kern_cold_up)) join_and(engines[kern_cold_up]) else "no engine"`, and the highest single kernel share is `r pct1(kern_top$kernel)` (`r kern_top$engine`, `r kern_top$cache` cache, `r lab_n(kern_top$rows)` rows). The data do not say what runs in the kernel; reading the files from the storage described above is a candidate (not tested here).

## Correctness

### Pushdown

```{r}
#| label: pushdown-table
if (nrow(pdf)) {
  pdt <- pdf[order(pdf$variant, pdf$table, pdf$rows), ]
  knitr::kable(data.frame(variant = pdt$variant, table = pdt$table, rows = lab_n(pdt$rows),
                          read = ifelse(pdt$plan == "pipeline", "whole pipeline", pdt$plan),
                          `columns read` = paste(pdt$n_read, "of", pdt$total_cols),
                          `row groups kept` = ifelse(is.na(pdt$row_groups_after_stats), paste("all", pdt$row_groups_total), paste(pdt$row_groups_after_stats, "of", pdt$row_groups_total)),
                          `rows decoded` = pct(pdt$rows_decoded / pdt$rows), `rows returned` = pct(pdt$rows_read / pdt$rows),
                          pushed = ifelse(nzchar(pdt$predicates), pdt$predicates, "none"),
                          check.names = FALSE), format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
}
```

The table is what `parquet_last_read()` reported after each cuplyr check run of the fact file. For the join pipeline the last read of the whole pipeline is the dimension file, so the table has a second row for it, from a run with the dimension computed first: the fact file is then the only parquet read of the plan, and the row shows its scan as it runs under the join. **Rows decoded** is the rows in the row groups kept after the statistics, from the file's metadata: the reader decodes whole row groups. **Rows returned** is what the scan hands on, after the pushed filter. `r push_sentence`

```{r}
#| label: push-ratio-table
prt <- data.frame(rows = lab_n(pn_size$rows), `row groups kept` = paste(pn_size$kept, "of", pn_size$total), `rows decoded` = pct(pn_size$decoded), check.names = FALSE)
for (e in engines) prt[[e]] <- fx(pn_size[[e]], 2)
knitr::kable(prt, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

The last four columns are the median time of the pushed variant divided by that of the other variant of the first pipeline (narrow table, warm cache).

## Rowwise

`r if (have_rw) rw_intro else rw_missing`

### The five forms

Each form is how its engine's users write it. The two dplyr forms and data.table read with the same arrow reader as the main pipelines, asking for the needed columns only (`r rw_needed_text`).

**cuplyr rowwise** reads with `read_parquet_gpu()`, makes the table rowwise with `rowwise()` and takes the per-row maximum and sum with `c_across()`. cuplyr does not evaluate these once per row: its rowwise support (F49) rewrites `max()` and `sum()` of `c_across()` into expressions across the columns (`rowwise_rewrite_dots()` in `R/rowwise.R`), so the GPU computes them over whole columns, as the vectorised forms do. If a rewrite is not possible the whole call falls back to dplyr on the CPU; whether this form stayed on the GPU is checked below (from F88's `cuplyr_cpu_fallback` condition, not guessed).

```{r}
#| label: code-rw-cuplyr
#| results: asis
code_block(src_nested(pp_rowwise_fn("cuplyr_rowwise")))
```

**dplyr rowwise** is the same verbs on a tibble: `rowwise()` and `c_across()`, which dplyr evaluates once per row.

```{r}
#| label: code-rw-dplyr
#| results: asis
code_block(src_nested(pp_rowwise_fn("dplyr_rowwise")))
```

**dplyr vectorised** is the expert's form, over whole columns with `pmax()` and `+`: the fair comparison for what a dplyr user would write. (The correctness reference for every form is a separate computation in base R; see below.)

```{r}
#| label: code-rw-dplyr-vec
#| results: asis
code_block(src_nested(pp_rowwise_fn("dplyr_vectorised")))
```

**data.table vectorised** uses `pmax()` and `rowSums()` over the columns, then an aggregate by `category`: the form this benchmark's brief names. `rowSums(.SD)` first copies the four columns into a matrix; adding them (`r paste0("\x60", paste(rw_cols, collapse = " + "), "\x60")`, as the dplyr and DuckDB forms do) would avoid that copy and may be faster. That form was not timed.

```{r}
#| label: code-rw-datatable
#| results: asis
code_block(src_nested(pp_rowwise_fn("datatable_vectorised")))
```

**DuckDB** is SQL over `read_parquet()` with explicit columns: `greatest()` and arithmetic, then a group by.

```{r}
#| label: code-rw-duckdb
#| results: asis
code_block(pp_rowwise_sql("<fact>.parquet"), "sql")
```

### How the rowwise calls were timed

The rules are those of the main pipelines (the section on how the calls were timed), except for which forms share a cell. `r rw_cells_text` In a cell the forms take turns in a rotating order, an untimed `gc()` precedes every call, warm and cold are the page cache of the wide file (`fincore` before every call, `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)` before every cold call), and a call is quiet when other processes' user-space CPU share is at most the same limit as everywhere else. `r rw_method_text` `r rw_gap_text` `r rw_sup_text`

Where the other form was capped, its time is above the cap and the ratio is bounded by cuplyr's median over the cap (shown as a bound).\n\n")

## First call

Each engine and variant ran in a fresh R process at `r lab_n(fc_rows[[1L]])` rows (narrow table, warm cache): the packages were loaded first (`load_secs`; for cuplyr that is `pkgload::load_all()` of the checkout, which is not what an installed package would pay), DuckDB's connection was opened, and then the calls ran one after another, each timed separately. A call is slow when it takes more than three times the median of the later half of the calls.

```{r}
#| label: first-call-table
fw <- stats::reshape(fc[fc$variant == "p1_push", c("engine", "call", "secs")], idvar = "engine", timevar = "call", direction = "wide")
names(fw) <- sub("^secs\\.", "call ", names(fw))
fw <- fw[match(engines, fw$engine), ]
fw$`load (s)` <- vapply(fw$engine, function(e) fc$load_secs[fc$engine == e][1L], 0)
for (j in seq_len(ncol(fw))) if (is.numeric(fw[[j]])) fw[[j]] <- fnum(fw[[j]])
knitr::kable(fw, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: first-call-summary
fs_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(engines, function(e) {
  d <- FC[FC$engine == e, ]
  data.frame(engine = e, `variants with a slow start` = sum(d$lead >= 1L), `slow calls (median)` = stats::median(d$lead),
             `first call, median (s)` = fnum(stats::median(d$first)), `later calls, median (s)` = fnum(stats::median(d$steady)),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(fs_tab, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: first-call-plot
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Seconds per call in a fresh process, by call number and variant"
d <- fc
d$engine <- factor(d$engine, engines)
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x = call, y = secs, colour = variant, group = variant)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() + ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(d$call))) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~engine, nrow = 1) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "call number in the process", y = "seconds", colour = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 10) + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

## Findings

### cuplyr's slow first calls of each new pipeline shape

`r first_finding` `r shapes_short`

The smallest repro found, in a fresh R process (the file is the benchmark's narrow table at `r if (have_shapes) lab_n(shapes_rows) else "n/a"` rows from `pp_gen_fact()`; the probe's calls took `r shapes_calls`, in this order):

```r
pkgload::load_all("."); library(dplyr)
f <- "fact-narrow-10000000.parquet"
for (i in 1:5) print(system.time(collect(read_parquet_gpu(f, columns = "store")))[["elapsed"]])
```

What the extra time is spent on is not examined here.

### A GPU left idle makes cuplyr's next call slower

`r idle_finding`

```{r}
#| label: idle-table
if (!is.null(idle_tab)) knitr::kable(idle_tab, format = "pipe", row.names = FALSE)
```

`r if (have_idle) paste0("A repro uses the probe's one-column scan", if (idle_scan_slowed) "" else " (in this data set the scan itself was not slowed by more than the factor above, so the rowwise form is the one that shows it)", ", in a fresh R process (the file is the benchmark's wide table at ", lab_n(idle_rows_n), " rows):") else "A repro, in a fresh R process (the file is the benchmark's wide table):"`

```r
pkgload::load_all("."); library(dplyr)
f <- "fact-wide-100000.parquet"
scan <- function() collect(read_parquet_gpu(f, columns = "x17"))
for (i in 1:3) scan()
for (idle in c(0, 10, 20, 40)) {
  Sys.sleep(idle)
  system("nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks.mem --format=csv,noheader")   # the memory clock, the measure the text uses
  print(c(idle = idle, secs = system.time(scan())[["elapsed"]]))
}
```

This is how the GPU behaves, not a wrong result; it is recorded for cuplyr and for anyone timing it, and nothing was changed. It is why dplyr rowwise has cells of its own here, and the caveats say what it means for the main cells.

### summarise() runs the plan at once in the first two pipelines

For the first and second pipelines (`r n_cu_early` of cuplyr's `r n_cu_cells` cells) the final `summarise()` runs the plan when it is called, because `max(qty)` is an integer `max()` whose result type depends on the data (F07). The GPU work happens inside `summarise()`, `collect()` only transfers the result, and a lazy table that ends in such a `summarise()` has nothing pending to inspect. This is not a wrong result and no timing here depends on it; it is recorded as a follow-up for cuplyr, and nothing was changed. A repro, in a fresh R process (the file is the benchmark's narrow table; `explain()` prints the pending operations of a lazy table):

```r
pkgload::load_all("."); library(dplyr)
f <- "fact-narrow-1000000.parquet"
x <- read_parquet_gpu(f) |> filter(qty >= 2L) |> group_by(store) |> summarise(m = max(qty))
explain(x)   # no pending operations: the plan ran inside summarise()
y <- read_parquet_gpu(f) |> filter(qty >= 2L) |> group_by(store) |> summarise(m = mean(qty))
explain(y)   # pending: summarise, filter and the parquet source
```

### The join of the second pipeline

`r join_sentence`

A repro of the join alone, on inputs that are already on the device (`stores.parquet` is the dimension from `pp_gen_dim()`; run it in a process that has already run the plan a few times, so that the first-call cost is out of it):

```r
pkgload::load_all("."); library(dplyr)
f <- "fact-narrow-100000000.parquet"
x <- read_parquet_gpu(f) |>
  filter(day >= as.Date("2024-01-01"), qty >= 2L) |>
  mutate(revenue = price * qty * (1 - discount)) |>
  select(store, channel, price, qty, revenue) |>
  compute()
d <- compute(read_parquet_gpu("stores.parquet"))
for (i in 1:5) print(system.time({ j <- compute(inner_join(x, d, by = "store")); cuplyr::gpu_sync() })[["elapsed"]])
```

## Caveats

- cuplyr runs with libcudf's debug stream pool switched on, which its `.onLoad` does by default since the second attempt at F85 (`LIBCUDF_USE_DEBUG_STREAM_POOL`, read back as `r setting("cuplyr", "debug_stream_pool")`). Every cuplyr number here includes that setting.
- F128 (the memory resource), F86 (transfers) and F87 (chunked streaming) may change cuplyr's numbers; this is a first set of measurements, to be repeated after they land.
- Other jobs on the machine. F123 was expected to share the machine with this benchmark; the lock log shows whether it did. `r lock_sentence`
- Process effects. `r shared_sentence`
- The GPU's idle cost (see Findings). `r gap_text`
- The rowwise chunk. `r rw_caveat`
- The first call. The tables are medians of warm-process calls after an untimed warm-up. In a fresh process, cuplyr's first call takes `r fs(stats::median(fc_cu$first))` and its later calls `r fs(stats::median(fc_cu$steady))` (median over the variants), and each new pipeline shape repeats part of that (see the first-call section); a script that runs each pipeline once is not what the tables measure.
- The data are sorted by date, which favours date pruning for any engine that uses row group statistics. Unsorted data would show less of the pushdown gap.
- DuckDB's local file caching is off by default (`cache_local_files` read back as `r setting("duckdb", "cache_local_files")`), so for DuckDB warm and cold mean the operating system's page cache, as for the others.
- One machine, one GPU, synthetic data, one codec (`r codec`), and the default thread counts of every engine; other settings or hardware will move the ratios.
